TIPP is a set of body-based distress-tolerance skills for moments when emotional arousal is so high that it is hard to think clearly, use more reflective skills, or choose what to do next. The immediate goal is not to solve the whole problem. The goal is to reduce the physical intensity enough to regain some choice. **Sometimes not making things worse is enough.** [1]

TIPP is especially useful when you notice very high activation, strong urges to act impulsively, or a sense that your body is driving the reaction. After the intensity comes down, you can decide what other skill fits the situation.

## TIPP at a glance {#tipp-at-a-glance}

| Skill | What you are trying to change | Learn more |
|---|---|---|
| **T - Temperature** | Use safe cooling of the face or upper cheeks to create a rapid body-level shift in high arousal. | [Temperature](temperature.qmd) |
| **I - Intense Exercise** | Use a short, safe burst of vigorous movement to use some of the physical energy that comes with high arousal. | [Intense Exercise](intense-exercise.qmd) |
| **P - Paced Breathing** | Slow the breath, breathe into the belly, and make the exhale a little longer than the inhale. | [Paced Breathing](paced-breathing.qmd) |
| **P - Progressive / Paired Muscle Relaxation** | Gently tense and release muscles while breathing so you can notice and reduce physical tension. | [Progressive Muscle Relaxation](progressive-muscle-relaxation.qmd) |

The four skills can be used separately. You do not need to complete all four every time. Choose the one that is safest, practical, and most likely to match what your body is doing.

## Temperature {#temperature}

Cooling the face can create a fast physiological shift when arousal is very high. The DBT handout describes using cool or cold water on the face, or placing a cold pack over the eyes and upper cheeks, while sitting quietly for a brief period. Facial cooling can trigger part of the body's diving response, which can slow the heart and change autonomic activity. [1]

This is a crisis-survival skill, not a test of how much cold you can tolerate. Use safe temperatures and brief exposure. [Read the Temperature page](temperature.qmd).

## Intense Exercise {#intense-exercise}

Strong emotion often comes with a strong physical activation signal. A short period of vigorous movement can give that activation somewhere to go. Examples can include fast walking, jogging, stairs, jumping, dancing, sports, or another activity that is appropriate for your body. [1]

The goal is a brief shift, not exhaustion, punishment, or pushing through pain. [Read the Intense Exercise page](intense-exercise.qmd).

## Paced Breathing {#paced-breathing}

Paced breathing slows the breathing rhythm and places more emphasis on the exhale. A common starting point is roughly five or six breaths per minute, with the exhale a little longer than the inhale. For example, you might breathe in for 4 or 5 counts and out for 6 or 7 counts. [1] Slow breathing has also been studied as a way of influencing autonomic regulation and subjective arousal. [2]

[Read the Paced Breathing page](paced-breathing.qmd).

## Progressive / Paired Muscle Relaxation {#progressive-muscle-relaxation}

Progressive or paired muscle relaxation teaches your body to notice the difference between tension and release. In the DBT version, you gently tense a muscle group while breathing in, then release the muscles as you breathe out. You can silently pair the release with a cue such as **relax** and notice the change in sensation. [1]

Practice tends to become easier when you first learn it in a quiet setting and then gradually use it in more ordinary environments. [Read the Progressive Muscle Relaxation page](progressive-muscle-relaxation.qmd).

::: {.callout-caution title="Physical safety"}
The Temperature and Intense Exercise parts of TIPP can affect heart rate and circulation. Use only approaches that are safe for your body. If you have a heart or circulation condition, a very low resting heart rate, significant cold sensitivity, take medication that affects heart rate, or have another medical concern, ask a qualified health professional before using these parts of TIPP. Stop if you feel faint, have chest pain, or feel physically unwell.
:::
